scenes.heading: Patterns of inheritance
scenes.sub: Predicting offspring with a simple grid
scenes.say: Breeders and genetic counsellors predict the chance of offspring having a trait. How? With a simple grid called a Punnett square.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Flip two coins: one in four chance of double tails
scenes.science: Tt × Tt: one in four chance of tt
scenes.breaks: Coins are always 50 : 50, but linked genes are partly stuck together, so some combinations turn up more often.
scenes.say: Each heterozygous parent is like a coin: heads for capital T, tails for little t. Flip two coins, and one outcome in four is double tails. So each child has a one in four chance of being little t little t. But a family of four won't always match. It's a probability for each child.
scenes.caption: Each heterozygous parent is like a coin: heads for T, tails for t. Flip two coins, and one outcome in four is double tails. So each child has a 1 in 4 chance of being tt. But a family of four won't always match. It's a probability for each child.

scenes.heading: Monohybrid cross
scenes.question: In mice, black fur (B) is dominant to brown (b). Two Bb mice are crossed. What proportion of offspring will be brown?
lines: Gametes: B or b from each parent
Punnett square: BB, Bb, Bb, bb
scenes.say: Two heterozygous black mice are crossed. Each parent makes capital B or little b gametes. The Punnett square gives one B B, two B b, and one b b. That's three black to one brown. So the chance of a brown mouse is one in four, or twenty-five percent.
scenes.caption: Two heterozygous black mice are crossed. Each parent makes B or b gametes. The Punnett square gives one BB, two Bb, and one bb. That's 3 black : 1 brown. So the chance of a brown mouse is 1 in 4, or 25%.

scenes.heading: Test cross
points: Cross the unknown with a homozygous recessive
Any recessive offspring: must be Tt
The recessive parent reveals the alleles
scenes.say: A dominant-looking organism could be homozygous or heterozygous. Cross it with a homozygous recessive. If any offspring show the recessive trait, the unknown parent must be heterozygous.

scenes.heading: Codominance vs incomplete

left.title: Codominance
points: Roan cattle: red AND white hairs
Like red and white scarves in a crowd

right.title: Incomplete dominance
points: Like mixing red and white paint

scenes.say: In codominance, both alleles show side by side, like roan cattle with separate red and white hairs. In incomplete dominance, the heterozygote is in between, like pink snapdragons. And blood groups? I A and I B are codominant, and both are dominant to little i.
scenes.caption: In codominance, both alleles show side by side, like roan cattle with separate red and white hairs. In incomplete dominance, the heterozygote is in between, like pink snapdragons. And blood groups? Iᴬ and Iᴮ are codominant, and both are dominant to i.

scenes.heading: X-linked inheritance
points: X-linked recessive: more common in males
Dad gives X to daughters, Y to sons
scenes.say: X-linked genes are on the X chromosome. Females have two X's, like owning a backup charger. Males have only one, so a recessive allele always shows. That's why haemophilia is more common in males. And a father never passes an X-linked allele to his son.

scenes.heading: Two genes at once
scenes.say: For two genes on different chromosomes, crossing two double heterozygotes gives nine to three to three to one. But linked genes ride in the same car. You get mostly parental types, and only a few recombinants from crossing over.
scenes.caption: For two genes on different chromosomes, RrYy × RrYy gives 9 : 3 : 3 : 1. But linked genes ride in the same car. You get mostly parental types, and only a few recombinants from crossing over.

points: X-linked recessive: more common in males
scenes.say: Quick recap. Two heterozygotes give three to one. A test cross reveals a hidden recessive allele. Codominance shows both; incomplete dominance blends. X-linked recessive traits are more common in males. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. Tt × Tt gives 3 : 1. A test cross reveals a hidden recessive allele. Codominance shows both; incomplete dominance blends. X-linked recessive traits are more common in males. Now try the practice questions!
